meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Confederation-level unitary jurisdiction; commercial register administration delegated to 26 cantonal Commercial Register Offices; candidate entity intended for Canton of Zug domiciliation)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romanistic-Germanic tradition; codified in the Swiss Civil Code and Code of Obligations; cantonal procedural variance in notarial practice and commercial register administration)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland-China Bilateral Investment Treaty of 16 June 1986 (in force 1987; replaced by the Switzerland-China BIT of 27 April 2009)
Switzerland-China Free Trade Agreement of 6 July 2013 (in force 1 July 2014)
Switzerland-China Double Taxation Agreement of 6 July 1990, as amended by the Protocol of 25 September 2010 (revised provisions effective 2013)
Switzerland-United States DTA of 2 October 1996, as amended by Protocol of 23 September 2011 (effective 1 October 2011)
Convention establishing the European Free Trade Association (EFTA, 1960), consolidated
Switzerland-European Union Free Trade Agreement of 22 July 1972

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) Arts. 626-639 (incorporation formalities of the Aktiengesellschaft, minimum capital, notarial deed); Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) Arts. 305bis-305ter (money laundering and deficiency in financial due diligence); Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing of 10 October 1997 (AMLA, SR 955.0), as revised in force since 1 January 2024; Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Persons and Legal Documents (SR 221.422, in force 1 January 2024) establishing the confidential federal Beneficial Owner Register; Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance of FINMA (AMLO-FINMA, SR 955.033); FINMA Circular 2020/01 (Client Due Diligence); Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411) Arts. 8-9 and 14-22; Federal Act on the Commercial Register (HRegG, SR 221.411).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (the federal Beneficial Owner Register is confidential, administered by the Federal Department of Justice and Police / Registry Authority; not publicly searchable; access limited to designated AML authorities such as MROS, FINMA, tax and criminal authorities, and regulated financial intermediaries performing KYC obligations; no public UBO transparency requirement exists in Switzerland)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial deed of incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde) including the Articles of Association (Statuten)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss cantonal notary public in the canton of incorporation (e.g., Notary of the Canton of Zug)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Executed and notarized exclusively in Switzerland; foreign-language charter exhibits (if any) must be certified-translated into German/French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of valid passport or national identity of each founder, board member and authorized signatory residing abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of the founder's home jurisdiction (passport office or civil registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent home jurisdiction authority, plus certified German/French/Italian (or English for bank-onboarding) translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal record / police clearance letter (extract) for each natural-person UBO, director and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country police, criminal registry or designated government authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Three-month bank reference / bank letter from a first-class regulated bank for each founder (source-of-funds and reputational vetting)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal relationship bank of the founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if required) or verified SWIFT-signed letter; translation certified if not in German/French/Italian

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner Declaration (declaration of economic beneficial ownership per AMLA Art. 4) and signed PEP/OFAC/UN sanctions self-certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each UBO, countersigned by the engagement legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature notarized by a Swiss notary or Swiss diplomatic/consular post abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate register extract / certificate of existence of any corporate founder entities (if any is used as a frontier shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille with certified translation; if the jurisdiction is not a Hague Convention party, full consular legalization of the documents at the competent Swiss embassy

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, shareholders and UBOs (25% threshold or control-based): (1) PEP classification per FATF definitions and FinSA Art. 12, including highest-institutional-function and family/close-associate profiling; (2) automated and manual screening against the UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (as implemented by Switzerland through SECO co-ordination), OFAC/SDN List, UK HMT sanctions list, and the Swiss SECO State Secretariat for Economic Affairs sanctions surveillance lists; (3) adverse-media and negative-news review of the principals in relevant professional databases; (4) enhanced due diligence notation if the tone at the top includes PEP status, politically exposed foreign residency, or source-of-wealth discrepancies, in line with FINMA Circular 2020/01.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Zentraler Firmenindex (Central Business Name Index), at www.zefix.ch, operated by the Federal Office of the Commercial Register in conjunction with the 26 cantonal Commercial Register Offices; formal name-reservation filings are routed through the competent cantonal Handelsregisteramt.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be presented in one of the official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian) or Romansh, or in Latin-script transliteration; the legal form indicator 'AG' (German) or 'SA' (French) is mandatory; foreign script (Cyrillic, Arabic, CJK) is not registered and must be transliterated into the Roman alphabet; names must not be misleading, must be distinctive, and must not imply a state/cantonal link or a licensed activity not actually held (Arts. 950-951 CO, Arts. 14, 27 HRegV).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bund / Eidgenossenschaft / Federal / Federal Council (requires Federal Chancellery authorization)
Schweizer / Swiss / Suisse / Svizzera (requires Swiss Intellectual Property Institute authorization and provable domestic economic nexus)
Kanton / Canton / Cantone (requires consent of the competent cantonal chancellery)
Bank / Banque / Banca (FINMA banking licence or Banks Act protected-term exemption)
Fonds / Investment Fund (CISA licensing and FINMA authorization)
Stiftung / Foundation (restricted to charitable or special-purpose structures under Civil Code Arts. 80-89b)
Treuhand / Fiduciaire / Fiduciary (restricted use in relation to the regulated fiduciary profession)
Rechtsanwalt / Attorney / Lawyer (reserved to licensed Swiss attorneys under the Federal Lawyers Act)
Revisor / Auditor / Prüfer (reserved to licensed audit firms)
Holding / Société de holding (requires company-group substantive evidence and is evaluated under misleading-name rules)
FinTech / Portfolio / Investment (accepted only if the business description in the Articles is precise and does not misleadingly suggest a supervised financial institution)
Zug / Crypto Valley (cantonal and geographical markers must not be misleading as to place of incorporation or commercial activity)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name-rejection notice from the cantonal Commercial Register Office, the applicant or its counsel may within 10 working days file an administrative objection with the cantonal supervisor of the Commercial Register; a further appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court (St. Gallen) under HRegV Art. 31 and ultimately to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court; the original name-reservation of 6 months can be extended once for an additional 6 months upon written justified request to the registry office; a modified name may be re-submitted at any time without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally acceptable. A purely virtual office without a physical Swiss berth is not permitted; however, licensed commercial domiciliation providers (administrative offices with physical Swiss infrastructure, service-of-process capacity and document registration) are widely accepted by cantonal Commercial Register Offices and FINMA-regulated banks for low-risk technology companies. The company must maintain demonstrable management substance in Switzerland, including books, board minutes, bank relationship and contract administration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: approximately 12%-18% probability of an unannounced physical inspection or information request within the first 12 months of registration, increasing to approximately 30%-35% if the registered office is a commercial domiciliation service or if the company links to multi-jurisdictional virtual-address providers; statutory basis for unannounced on-site checks exists under AMLA Arts. 20-22 for regulated financial intermediaries and under cantonal tax/commercial-register enforcement powers.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing cantonal notarial tariff for an Aktiengesellschaft with minimum capital; estimated CHF 1,000, converted at 1.15 USD/CHF

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official Commercial Register registration fee (entry of the AG, legal-form filings and review)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) with the federal share to the Federal Office of the Commercial Register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Federal Commercial Register tariff plus cantonal surcharge; estimated CHF 1,100 total

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance request and 6-month reservation via the Zefix portal / cantonal registry review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Nominal statutory tariff for the request of an official name reservation (CHF 40-60)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and consular legalization of foreign documents (passports, police certificates, bank reference letters, corporate extracts - estimated 4-6 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authorities of the home jurisdiction, and Swiss diplomatic/consular posts only where a non-Hague state is involved
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-document apostille fee benchmark (approx. CHF 30-60 per document) plus courier handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translations (German/French/Italian) of foreign registry documents and due diligence exhibits
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of CHF 100-150 per page for sworn certified translation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation service - first annual term (physical berth, service of process, mail acceptance, compliance correspondence)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark CHF 275-325 per month for a low-risk fintech corporate office package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration preparation and PEP / OFAC / UN / SECO sanctions screening of all principals (automated and analyst-assisted)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Engaged legal counsel and compliance data provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat professional fee of CHF 500 including database charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due-diligence work, drafting of articles of association, AML/CFT onboarding questionnaire and commercial register submission
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss business law / international tax law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of CHF 375 per hour, estimated 8-10 hours for a standard low-risk AG dossier

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Capital deposit confirmation from a Swiss bank (opening of a blocked 'Kapital einzahlung' account and issuance of the confirmation letter for the notary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank in Switzerland (entity relationship to be formed)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff for private-account deposit and confirmation letter; estimated CHF 200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official gazette publication fee in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) and contingent cantonal charges
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) and cantonal registry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory minimum share capital reserve - CHF 100,000 callable capital, CHF 20,000 minimum paid-in by cash at incorporation (informational; not a P&L expense; held in blocked bank account until registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: The entity's first Swiss bank relationship (blocked account regime)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory minimum capital requirement of the Code of Obligations Art. 632 (not a fee; zero-cost compliance line for completeness)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 620–763 (Aktiengesellschaft); Art. 628 (incorporators' declaration), Art. 629 (audit confirmation), Art. 632 (minimum capital and paid-up requirement), Arts. 716a–716b (non-transferable board duties), Arts. 640–643 (registered shares)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), supervised by the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office (EHRA/FEDRO); filings published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsakt) incorporating the Articles of Association (Statuten) and the incorporators' declaration, filed electronically with the Commercial Register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000 (approx. USD 112,000); at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up as cash (20% of each share's par value, capped at CHF 50,000) and deposited in a blocked capital-clearance account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss-chartered bank in the company's name, released only upon Commercial Register issuance per Art. 632 OR.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: This First Board Resolution is adopted by the incorporators of CH_AG acting as the provisional board of directors under Art. 628 OR. 1. Share Subscription: The Board confirms subscription of 100 registered shares at CHF 1,000 par value, totaling CHF 100,000, of which CHF 50,000 is deposited in a blocked capital-clearance account at a Swiss bank. 2. Registered Office: The registered office is set at Bahnhofstrasse 21, 6300 Zug, Switzerland. 3. Officers: The Board appoints [Name] as Chairperson, [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, and [Name] as Secretary, each with individual signature. 4. Filing: The Board instructs the notary and auditor to file this deed with the Zug Commercial Register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Association and Incorporation Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Canton of Zug (and coordinating fiduciary advisor)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association (Statuten) in accordance with Art. 626 OR, stating corporate purpose (development and operation of personal wealth analytics and investment tracking software; performance of IT services), share capital, share categories, registered office, and board composition. Appear personally or by power of attorney before the cantonal notary to authenticate the incorporation declaration, confirming capital subscription, absence of non-cash contributions (Sacheinlagen), and lawful corporate purpose. The notary will attest the deed and transmit an electronic extract to the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association (Statuten) in German (or authorized French/English translation)
Incorporation declaration with capital subscription schedule (Art. 628 OR)
Passport or identity card copies of all incorporators, board members, and authorized signatories
Declaration of no qualified participation under Art. 628a OR (confirmation of lawful funds)
Written consent forms of each board member and the licensed auditor
Notarized power of attorney if incorporator is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or preliminary registry review queries the Articles (e.g., incomplete corporate purpose or defective capital clause), amend the Statuten and re-notarize; the initial deed can be corrected by an addendum without losing filing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account and Deposit of Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss-chartered bank (e.g., UBS, Credit Suisse, Zuger Kantonalbank) — not a state authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account (Sperrkonto) in the name of CH_AG with the chosen bank, depositing at least CHF 50,000. Instruct the bank to issue a formal capital-clearance confirmation (Freigabeerklärung / confirmation of paid-up share capital) addressed to the Commercial Register, acknowledging that the funds are irrevocably at the company's disposal and will only be released upon presentation of the Commercial Register excerpt evidencing registration.
required_dossiers: Certified extract of the notarized deed or draft Articles
Account application and client due-diligence forms (beneficial ownership declaration)
Passport copies and proof of residence of incorporators/beneficial owners
Confirmation of bank account-receiving instructions
Deposit receipt or SWIFT confirmation for CHF 50,000
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the blocked-account confirmation due to incomplete KYC documentation, supply certified identity documents and source-of-funds evidence; alternatively, use another Swiss-chartered bank and re-issue the deposit confirmation without reopening the notarized capital clause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Filing to the Cantonal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), via the e-GRIS electronic filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, the incorporators' declaration, the auditor's confirmation of due formation (Art. 629 OR), the bank's capital-clearance confirmation, and specimen signature cards for all board members and officers. The registrar examines legal conformity, identity, capital certification, and compliance with Art. 630 OR; upon approval, the company is registered and the registry issues a constitutive effect with legal personality as of the registration date.
required_dossiers: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (electronic transmission by notary)
Auditor's report confirming proper formation and minimum capital (Art. 629 OR)
Blocked-account capital clearance from the Swiss bank
Deed of resignation or consent of any third-party authorized signatories
Specimen signatures of the board chairperson, CEO, and secretary
Commercial Register application form and proof of fee payment (approx. CHF 800)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a deficiency notice (Mängelrüge), rectify the identified defects within the statutory deadline (typically 30 days); if registration is refused, appeal to the Cantonal Supervision Authority over Commercial Registers within 10 days of the refusal decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Gazette and Issuance of Commercial Register Excerpt and UID
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB) and the Federal Statistical Office (BfS) for the UID
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the Commercial Register automatically transmits the company data to SHAB for mandatory publication (Art. 931 OR). Simultaneously, the Federal Statistical Office assigns the Swiss business identifier (UID / Identifikationsnummer). Retrieve the official Commercial Register excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug) via Zefix or the cantonal portal to evidence legal existence for bank account activation, auditor appointment, and contract execution.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt request (online Zefix query)
Registration confirmation and UID certificate issued by the registry
SHAB publication notice
Proof of registered office address and mail-forwarding instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SHAB publication or UID issuance is delayed, file a trace request with the Commercial Register; if the published data contains errors, submit a correction application (Berichtigungsgesuch) to the registrar, who will republish the corrected entry at no additional statutory fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Federal and Cantonal Registrations (Tax, Social Security, and Insurance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA); Zug Cantonal Tax Office (Dienststelle Steuern); AHV Compensation Office Zug; Suva (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with the FTA for VAT (obligatory at CHF 100,000 annual turnover; voluntary registration permitted within 30 days of incorporation), and with the cantonal tax office for profit tax, corporate capital tax, and withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends and interest. Register as an employer with the AHV compensation office and obtain the employer number; register for compulsory accident insurance with Suva (non-occupational accident insurance normally mandatory for employees).
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt and UID confirmation
FTA VAT registration form (Formular 101 / e-services)
Cantonal tax registration questionnaire and corporate structural data
AHV employer registration form with payroll details
Suva registration application and workplace description
Occupational pension fund (BVG) registration declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration penalties can be waived if good cause is shown; file all social security and tax forms retroactively to the registration date, and request a payment plan for any computed back taxes or AHV contributions to avoid enforcement proceedings.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Building and Fire Safety Inspectorate of Zug (Feuerpolizei Zug) and the Cantonal Labor Inspectorate for workplace compliance; no sector-specific industrial license applies to pure software development and financial portfolio tracking under ISIC 6201
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license required for fintech software-as-a-service activities; physical office premises require a standard occupancy permit (Gebrauchsbewilligung) under Zug building regulations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based software operations fall outside the scope of mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment under the Swiss EIA Ordinance (UVPV/ÖIAV); no environmental permit is required for the company's registered office of 100–200 m² in Zug
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic wastewater must be discharged into the public sewer in accordance with the Federal Water Protection Act (GSchG, Art. 7), with municipal pre-treatment standards; cooling and ventilation systems must not release refrigerants contrary to the Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance (ChemRRV); electronic waste (servers, end-user devices) must be disposed of via the Swiss take-back system under the Ordinance on the Return, Take-Back and Disposal of Electrical and Electronic Equipment (ORD/VDESA); if on-site power generation or coating processes are later added, VOC thresholds of the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) would apply — none currently triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from Zug Fire Police for office occupancy, comprising emergency exit signage, fire extinguisher servicing, evacuation plan, and annual inspection certificate; structural load inspection certified by the cantonal building authority through the occupancy permit; occupational safety clearance per Suva and the Labor Ordinance 3, including ergonomic workplace assessments, electrical installation inspection (low-voltage installations per NIV), and a written safety concept (Sicherheitskonzept) if more than 50 employees are employed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV/FTA), Main Division Value Added Tax, Bern; official portal: www.estv.admin.ch. Customs and export-declaration competence: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (Bundesamt für Zoll und Grenzsicherheit, BAZG; www.bazg.admin.ch). Central electronic Commercial Register and UID database: Zefix (www.zefix.ch).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss AG obtains the unified business identifier (UID) automatically upon entry in the cantonal Commercial Register; VAT registration is completed via the FTA's online VAT registration form, which activates the UID with the 'MWST' suffix (format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX MWST) within approximately 14-30 days. Non-resident foreign entities without a Swiss seat register directly with the FTA (no domestic registered office required) by submitting constitutive documents, AML/KYC identification of beneficial owners and legal representatives, and a declaration of expected Swiss-source turnover; they receive a UID-MWST for VAT filing and for the simplified VAT refund procedure. Registration with the competent cantonal tax administration is additionally required where a Swiss permanent establishment is maintained. For the ISIC 6201 financial portfolio-tracking software activity (non-banking fintech, AML low-risk tier, no statutory license), no other federal tax license applies; the same registration path governs resident AG and foreign branch alike.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (an Aktiengesellschaft is a separate, non-transparent tax subject for federal, cantonal and communal profit and capital taxes; residence-based worldwide taxation applies, subject to the territorial carve-out exemption for foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate under Art. 52 DBG; no pass-through or flow-through classification is available).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Switzerland; tax classification is fixed by legal form. Available statutory elections and reliefs: (i) participation relief (Beteiligungsabzug) on dividends and capital gains from qualifying participations (≥10% or acquisition value ≥ CHF 1 million); (ii) notional interest deduction on qualifying surplus equity (Art. 25a DBG, introduced by the Swiss Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act); (iii) cantonal patent-box and additional R&D super-deduction options under the STAF framework; (iv) VAT small-business exemption election below CHF 100,000 turnover (Art. 11 VAT Act); and (v) VAT group taxation election for closely integrated entities (Art. 21 VAT Act). Hybrid-mismatch deduction disallowance is applied under Art. 58a DBG, aligning Swiss law with BEPS Action 2.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT; German: Mehrwertsteuer; French: taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) under the Swiss Federal Act on Value Added Tax of 12 June 2009 (SR 641.20), administered by the FTA.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies (Art. 10(2)(a) VAT Act); non-established suppliers of services placed in Switzerland (including B2C e-services) are subject to registration once Swiss-source turnover exceeds CHF 100,000; below-threshold businesses may elect small-business exemption, forfeiting input VAT deduction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous-transaction-control or digital stamping mandate exists at the Swiss federal level. B2B e-invoicing is voluntary but standardized via the Swiss QR-Invoice (QR-Rechnung) and the PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0 network; suppliers to the Swiss federal administration must transmit e-invoices through the mandated federal e-billing channel. VAT returns and refund claims are filed electronically via the FTA portal; all VAT records and source documents must be retained for 10 years for tax-audit access.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% with preservation of the input VAT deduction applies to tangible goods physically exported from Swiss customs territory and to services directly related to such exports (freight, handling, dispatch) under Art. 23(1) VAT Act. For the ISIC 6201 cloud portfolio-tracking software activity, cross-border supplies are generally outside the Swiss VAT scope: B2B services sold to non-resident principals are localized at the recipient's place of business (Art. 8 VAT Act), and B2C digital services are ex-Swiss when not effectively used or benefited in Switzerland; both treatments are economically equivalent to 0% with full input VAT recovery. Eligibility requires verifiable evidence of both the cross-border movement (goods) and the recipient's foreign seat or foreign place of benefit (services).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (e-dec / Ausfuhrbeleg or official Ausfuhrzollanmeldung) discharged by the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (BAZG) proving physical removal of the goods from Swiss customs territory
Transport and dispatch documentation evidencing cross-border carriage: Bill of Lading, Sea Waybill, CMR consignment note, or Air Waybill, together with the carrier delivery receipt

Inward remittance certificate: commercial invoice, bank credit advice, and payment-flow records for the export proceeds (Switzerland requires no statutory FX-repatriation certificate, but banking-settlement evidence is mandatory substantiation in FTA export audits)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The FTA conducts documentary post-audits of zero-rated export transactions; an unsubstantiated zero-rating claim is re-assessed at the standard 8.1% rate with default interest at 4.5% p.a. and a full clawback of correspondingly deducted input VAT. Negligent or wilful evasion triggers administrative fines of up to three times the tax evaded and criminal prosecution in serious cases (Art. 96-97 VAT Act); the statutory assessment and recovery period extends to 10 years in evasion scenarios (Art. 89 VAT Act), during which all records must be retained. Switzerland maintains no statutory FX-repatriation deadline and has no exchange controls; the 180-day parameter is the documentary-settlement benchmark for export invoice ageing and credit recycling in FTA and banking practice.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB), in coordination with the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) of the Federal Department of Finance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility on both current and capital account transactions under the OECD Code of Liberalisation. There are no exchange control statutes, no licensing requirements for inbound or outbound remittances, and no SNB approval gates for dividend, interest, royalty, or equity flows. The Swiss franc is a freely traded reserve currency. Profit remittance hurdles are fiscal rather than regulatory: dividends face a 35% anticipatory withholding tax automatically refundable or reduced under applicable double taxation treaties; otherwise, no administrative convertibility or repatriation barrier exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation timeline for export service receipts. An exporting or cross-border SaaS company may retain export proceeds indefinitely in freely convertible currency in domestic or multi-currency accounts; conversion into CHF or any other currency is entirely at the company's discretion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium, ancillary only. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise Business or Revolut Business are not licensed in Switzerland, do not offer legally segregated client funds under Swiss Banking Act (BA), and are unacceptable as the primary treasury spine of a Swiss AG. A regulated European EMI can be used as a supplementary EUR collection rail, while the main operating account, share-capital escrow, FX hedging, and liquidity clearing must remain with a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors must undergo a personal AML/KYC interview. Tier-1 institutions (UBS, ZKB, ZGKB) typically require at least one physical appearance by a director or a board-authorized Swiss signatory at a Swiss branch, or a certified remote video identification process only for Low_Risk_Standard, non-PEP clients of digitally native banks. Physical presence in Switzerland remains the practical norm and materially accelerates onboarding; a remote-only opening for a foreign-resident board is possible but will attract enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated AG with non-Swiss-resident beneficial owner and a digital-only revenue model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized deed of incorporation, current Commercial Register excerpt, articles of association, board resolution on account mandate, complete shareholder and beneficial-ownership register, apostilled passport and proof of address of each UBO, banking reference letter, six-month source-of-funds statements traceable to the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital, confirmation of the paid-up CHF 50,000 via transparent wire, Swiss VAT registration certificate and a business model narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fintech 'financial portfolio tracking' app potentially classified as regulated financial services under FinSA or AMLA
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss counsel legal opinion confirming freedom from banking, FinSA, and AMLA licensing; FINMA negative activity confirmation or negative ruling if requested; Terms of Use stating the application is analytical software only and does not provide investment advice, custody, order transmission, or payment transfer; evidence that revenue derives solely from App Store subscriptions and Stripe SaaS fees; proof of no client money handling beyond ordinary subscription billing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume low-value Stripe and Apple IAP settlements flagged for layering or unlicensed payment activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant agreements with Stripe and Apple App Store, monthly payout reconciliation statements, audited income statement mapping inflows to subscription sales, user analytics and chargeback history, Swiss MWST (VAT) filings, geographical customer breakdown, and banking transaction monitoring clarification confirming all receipts correspond to genuine SaaS subscriptions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency or Web3 association due to the Zug Crypto Valley location
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board attestation that the company never accepts, holds, or settles in digital assets or tokens; treasury policy showing fiat-only clearing; transaction monitoring report evidencing zero crypto counterparties; technical architecture description demonstrating the absence of wallets, blockchain nodes, or crypto-payment modules; company branding audited to avoid implied distributed-ledger activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP exposure, unseen legal-owner chain, or shareholder in a higher-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete beneficial ownership declaration per Swiss AMLO Form BO; organizational chart up to ultimate individuals; certified business background statement; independent third-party background screening reports; sanctions screening consent and negative results; written undertaking to deliver annual shareholder confirmations and to notify the bank of any ownership change.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections must be executed via SWIFT MT103 using the payment purpose 'Equity Share Capital / Unrestricted Paid-in Capital' under Swiss Form A and OCO coding for cross-border remittance statistics, referencing the shareholder name and the company's Swiss corporate identifier. Funds are credited to the blocked Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto), with upfront bank attestation sent to the Commercial Register confirming the capital is at the board's free disposal. Post-incorporation intercompany injections use purpose code 'Intercompany Loan / Equity Contribution', accompanied by a certified loan agreement or capital increase protocol; no SNB approval is required, but all wiring, purpose-code, and supporting documents are retained for fiscal and transfer-pricing inspection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and operating disbursements are executed through SWIFT MT103 for non-European counterparties and through SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR or Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) for domestic and EEA flows. For material cloud-infrastructure or hardware procurements involving multi-million CHF values, Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 are recommended as secure trade-clearing rails. Stripe and Apple App Store IAP settle in CHF or EUR directly into the CHF operational account; residual USD and EUR balances are held in multi-currency sub-accounts or converted via FX forwards to fund the next operating cycle.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX forward contracts (CHF/USD and CHF/EUR)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) to hedge emerging-market currency receipt positions that are not freely deliverable outside the counterparty jurisdiction
Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) to swap USD and EUR liquidity into CHF while covering principal, interest, and duration risk
FX options and zero-cost collars to protect large Apple IAP settlement spikes against adverse CHF appreciation
FX swaps used for short-term liquidity matching between the multi-currency sub-accounts and the CHF operating account

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) approval of annual financial statements, profit appropriation, discharge of board members, and signed AGM minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' General Meeting; executed minutes retained at registered office; no commercial register filing required for purely domestic non-listed annual account approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM within six months after balance-sheet date; for calendar-year companies by 30 June; annual report and audit report, if any, must be available to shareholders at the registered office at least 20 days before the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director liability and criminal fines for failure to hold the AGM or to produce annual accounts; shareholders or creditors may petition a court to order convocation; persistent default can lead to statutory rectification and eventual deregistration after formal notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss direct federal and cantonal tax return (profit tax and equity/capital tax) with the AGM-approved annual financial statements annexed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration and Swiss Federal Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Cantonal filing deadline commonly 30 June after balance-sheet date for calendar-year companies; extended filing to 31 December is generally available through a qualified tax representative or electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default tax assessment, late-payment and late-filing interest, penalty surcharges, director liability for unpaid corporate taxes, and, in aggravated cases, collection and dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss VAT return, if the company is VAT-registered or has opted into VAT liability
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration, VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual VAT return due within 60 days after the end of the annual VAT assessment period; a quarterly or semi-annual filing plan applies if turnover thresholds require it
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, default interest, VAT fines for negligent or intentional underdeclaration, director liability, and criminal proceedings in serious cases

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Auditor's report (ordinary audit or limited review) or valid unanimous shareholder opt-out resolution confirming an audit waiver
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at the AGM; audit report retained at the registered office; no commercial register filing of the audit report is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor's report must be available to shareholders with the annual report at least 20 days before the AGM; any auditor appointment or resignation involving register-relevant data must be notified to the commercial register within 14 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors personally liable for failing to obtain a required statutory audit or valid opt-out; criminal fines may apply; shareholders or creditors may petition a court to appoint an auditor

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Event-driven commercial register mutation filings, including changes of board members, signatories, registered office, share capital, corporate purpose, and liquidation steps
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Registrations and notifications generally due within 14 calendar days after the underlying resolution or event; no separate annual commercial register return applies to a Swiss AG
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines for late filing, lack of third-party reliance for unregistered facts, director penalties, and, after repeated non-compliance, commercial register rectification with possible liquidation and strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Swiss AG is subject to ordinary statutory audit if, in two consecutive financial years, at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded: total assets above CHF 20 million; net turnover above CHF 40 million; annual average of more than 250 full-time employees. Ordinary audit is also required for listed companies and entities making public offers of securities. Otherwise, the company may undergo a limited review by a licensed auditor or be entirely audit-exempt if all shareholders consent and the company does not exceed 10 full-time employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations statutory accounting principles (OR arts. 957-962); Swiss GAAP FER is the recognized national interpretation; IFRS may be used as a supplementary reporting framework, and statutory tax accounts remain based on OR-compliant records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not require an annual public UBO declaration to the commercial register. The board must keep the Aktienbuch (shareholder register) and, where applicable, a beneficial-owner record reflecting natural-person control of 25% or more of capital or voting rights. Share transfers must be recorded in the shareholder register before the transferee may exercise shareholder rights. The corporate secretary should perform an annual reconciliation of the shareholder register, board and signatory lists, transfer records, and UBO records, and file any necessary mutation notices arising from inconsistencies.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of directors, signatories, and statutory auditor (internal corporate register)
Corporate minute book containing general meeting and board resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CHF 1,000-5,000 per annum, approximately USD 1,100-5,600, for a Swiss corporate-services registered office and statutory agent/secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0-4,800 for an audit-exempt micro AG; USD 3,300-11,000 for a limited review; USD 16,000-54,000 for a full ordinary audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax share; combined federal + cantonal/communal headline rate normally ranges from 11.8% to 21.1% depending on the canton of registered office (e.g., approximately 14.9% for Zug, 21.1% for Zurich)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss STAF (Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act) provides: (i) super deduction of 150% for qualifying research and development expenditures; (ii) patent box regime allowing partial deduction of qualifying intellectual property income, subject to a maximum tax relief cap; (iii) optional notional interest deduction on qualifying equity if adopted by the canton; (iv) participation relief exempting 95% to 100% of dividend income and capital gains from qualifying participations of at least 10%; (v) no statutory digital services tax for software and fintech activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss combined cantonal and federal corporate tax return for legal entities (Steuererklärung juristische Personen / Déclaration fiscale des personnes morales), including the federal direct tax annex. Filed electronically via the cantonal tax authority's e-portal using authorised software (e.g., Zug e-portal, Zurich eServices, or equivalent cantonal system).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly instalment payments may be required for below-year or anticipated tax liabilities, but the return itself is filed once per fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The cantonal tax authority sends the pre-completed return; for an AG, the filing deadline is normally 60 days after receipt of the form, extendable to no later than 30 September after a calendar-year fiscal year-end (or within six months after a non-calendar year-end), subject to canton-specific rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Company identification and registered office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter legal name, commercial register number, registered office address, date of incorporation, fiscal year-end, main business activity (ISIC/NACE code), and tax ID.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable as a personal entry; the Swiss AG must indicate whether direct or indirect non-resident shareholders exist in the shareholding schedule. No direct foreign filing obligation appears here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach final statutory balance sheet, income statement, and notes; reconcile commercial accounting results to tax basis in the annexed tax reconciliation schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The AG must ensure that transactions with non-resident shareholders (loans, service fees, royalties, cost recharges) are fully disclosed in the annexed schedules if they exceed materiality thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State commercial profit after Swiss GAAP or IFRS, adjusted for non-deductible expenses (e.g., excessive management remuneration contrary to arm's length standard) and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident beneficial owner cannot enter this section; the resident AG is the sole taxpayer. Expenses paid to non-resident related parties must satisfy the arm's length standard or be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim the participation exemption on qualifying dividend income and capital gains from shareholdings of at least 10% (or CHF 1 million nominal value); enter the percentage of participation and gross amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident parent holds 10% or more, the AG must attach the parent company's address, ownership percentage, and proof of holding to evidence the relief. No relief is available if the shareholder is domiciled in a non-cooperative jurisdiction without substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete the R&D annex and enter the additional 50% deduction on qualifying Swiss R&D personnel costs and third-party R&D mandates (total deduction of 150% of qualifying costs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For R&D contracts with non-resident affiliates, the AG must retain full functional and risk analysis, cost breakdowns, and comparability data; only Swiss-performed R&D (including R&D performed in a Swiss branch of the AG) qualifies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: If the AG owns or development-qualified patents, enter the deductibility of net IP income under the Swiss patent box and attach the nexus calculation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nexus documentation must prove qualifying development expenditures; a cost-sharing arrangement with a non-resident IP company requires a transfer pricing analysis; otherwise, the patent box is denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset prior-year tax losses up to the statutory seven-year period; attach the loss register with loss years, amounts, and set-off dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses are ring-fenced to the Swiss AG. A non-resident shareholder or related foreign branch cannot offset its own losses against Swiss AG profits under normal rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section F – Tax prepayments and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter prepaid instalments for federal and cantonal tax, plus any creditable foreign tax on Swiss-permanent-establishment profits or foreign-source dividends subject to limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding taxes are not directly creditable in the Swiss return unless they relate to income of a Swiss permanent establishment; the non-resident shareholder handles foreign tax credits in its home jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: federal procedural fine up to CHF 10,000; cantonal procedural fine typically up to CHF 5,000; if the return is filed or the case cannot be assessed, the tax authority may issue a default assessment with a surcharge of up to 100% of tax. In addition, default interest runs at 4.5% per annum on the unpaid tax; further coercive penalties and daily surcharges (zwangsweise Durchsetzung) may be imposed until the return is submitted.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% statutory Swiss withholding tax on dividends distributed by a Swiss AG, regardless of residency of the shareholder, subject to tax treaty relief or tax exemption in certain domestic cases.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Swiss AG withholding agent must remit 35% to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA). A non-resident shareholder claiming treaty relief must file a refund application on FTA Form 82 within three years of the due date of the withholding tax, attaching: (i) an original tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's home tax authority, not more than one year old; (ii) evidence of dividend entitlement and payment; (iii) a beneficial ownership declaration; and if applicable, (iv) a completed FTA Form 823 for release at source for subsequent distributions. For parent companies in a DTA state, the Swiss AG may apply to the FTA in advance for a withholding tax release at the source using Form 823, supported by the parent's TRC and a confirmation of minimum ownership (usually 10%) where not domestic exemption applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% Swiss withholding tax under domestic law; most Swiss DTAs either exempt or cap royalty taxation in the source state at 0%-10% (source state follows the DTA). Interest: interest on ordinary intercompany loans and bank deposits is outside the definition of Swiss dividend and bond interest, thus 0% withholding; interest on Swiss publicly issued bonds and money market instruments remains subject to 35% statutory withholding, reduced to 0%-10% under applicable DTAs.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CHF 500,000 (recommended audit threshold); CHF 900,000,000 for mandatory Master File/CbCR group threshold
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but it enforces a functional substance concept derived from OECD treaty-residency principles and Swiss tax-case law. An AG must maintain a real office, locally available books and records, substantive board activity, personnel with decision-making authority, and genuine economic risk-taking in Switzerland. A letter-box AG may be denied treaty benefits, temporary reliefs, and the patent box; the tax authority may reattribute profits to the foreign parent or deem hidden profit distributions, resulting in additional 35% withholding tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (federal and cantonal direct tax)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting taxable income, dummy legal entities, concealed digital asset transactions, false or manipulated records, or intentionally charging non-arm's length management fees to a non-resident parent to shift Swiss profits abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Swiss Federal Direct Tax Act (DBG), tax evasion entails a fine of up to 100% of the tax evaded (federal and cantonal portions); for aggravated false-document tax fraud, the fine may increase to three times the tax evaded and ordinary criminal fines up to CHF 36,000, or imprisonment up to three years in serious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managing officers are personally, jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid taxes and penalties if they committed, directed, or authorised the evasion. Travel bans may be imposed within Swiss debt collection proceedings, and imprisonment of up to three years applies for intentional fraudulent tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repeated late filing, failure to disclose related-party transactions, obstruction of tax audit, or ignoring administrative surcharges and final deadline warnings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal procedural fine of up to CHF 10,000; cantonal fine of up to CHF 5,000; risk of ex officio assessment with a security surcharge of up to 100% of the tax base; default interest of 4.5% per annum on all overdue amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The entire board of directors can be held individually responsible for the administrative duties of the AG; failure to comply after a formal order may lead to personal fines and coercive detention (maximum eight weeks) until the documents are produced.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Swiss AG merely as a domicile vehicle for portfolio tracking with no office, staff, bank account, or operational activity, particularly where non-resident customers contract through the AG to attract lower Swiss taxes or treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, withdrawal of patent box and participation relief; income is recharacterised and allocated to the parent jurisdiction; deemed dividend distributions subject to 35% Swiss withholding tax; regulatory authorities may compel striking off the Commercial Register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly maintain a shell AG are jointly liable for unpaid taxes and WHT on deemed distributions; they may be banned from board positions in Switzerland and are subject to criminal penalties for false declarations in commercial register filings.
